data.description:
## Description

What: New PreToolUse hook plugins/dso/hooks/check-pr-destructive-action.sh that parses the Bash tool command string and blocks any invocation containing 'gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)' that does not also contain 'pr-destructive-action.sh'; plus the CLAUDE.md 'Never Do These' rule 25 in negative-directive form documenting the prohibition, the exit-code contract (0/1/2/3), and the rationale (session ownership; see fe66-f05b). Why: This hook is the load-bearing enforcement that makes the negative directive structural. Scope IN: the hook with its command-string parse-and-block logic; a hook integration test asserting the block fires on direct 'gh pr close N' and does NOT fire on 'pr-destructive-action.sh N close'; the CLAUDE.md rule-25 text. Scope OUT: the wrapper itself (draft-4); SKILL.md call-site rewrites (draft-7).


## Done Definitions

- check-pr-destructive-action.sh blocks a Bash command containing 'gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)' that does not also contain 'pr-destructive-action.sh', and allows commands that route through the wrapper ← Satisfies: sc-4
- A hook integration test asserts the block fires on a direct 'gh pr close N' invocation and does NOT fire on a 'pr-destructive-action.sh N close' invocation ← Satisfies: sc-4
- CLAUDE.md 'Never Do These' rule 25 states the negative directive (never invoke gh pr destructive directly; use pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path; blocked by check-pr-destructive-action.sh), documents the 0/1/2/3 exit-code contract, and cites the session-ownership rationale (fe66-f05b) ← Satisfies: sc-4
- The hook does NOT allow a Bash command that merely CONTAINS the literal string pr-destructive-action.sh while still reaching a raw destructive gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment): the hook verifies the destructive gh pr token is actually the wrapper-invoked form, not a co-located, compound-separated, or quoted/heredoc/comment mention. Negative-adversarial fixtures — (a) co-location bypass 'echo pr-destructive-action.sh && gh pr close 5', (b) compound-statement separation ('pr-destructive-action.sh ...; gh pr merge 7'), (c) heredoc/comment mention of pr-destructive-action.sh preceding a raw gh pr edit — are all BLOCKED, while a genuine 'pr-destructive-action.sh 5 close' is ALLOWED ← Satisfies: sc-4

## Considerations

- [LoadBearing] This hook is the structural enforcement; the SKILL.md negative directives (draft-7) are documentation, not enforcement — the hook must fire regardless of whether SKILL.md text is followed.
- [Parsing] The command-string parser must handle compound commands (pipes, &&, subshells) so a destructive gh pr buried in a compound invocation is still blocked.
- [Doc-test] The CLAUDE.md rule-25 DD is verified by behavioral content assertion (regex on required tokens), not by diffing the file.
- [Adversarial] sc-4 structural premise: a substring-presence allow-check is defeatable. The allow-condition must establish that the destructive gh pr token is the argument of an actual pr-destructive-action.sh invocation (the wrapper-invoked form) — not that the wrapper name appears anywhere in the command string. Treat co-location, compound separation (&&, ;, |, subshells), and quoted/heredoc/comment mentions as bypasses to block.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I want a PreToolUse hook that blocks any direct gh pr destructive invocation not routed through pr-destructive-action.sh, plus the CLAUDE.md rule-25 negative directive
